articles.title: Google Alarmed by Formidable AI-Powered Zero-Day Cyberattack
articles.summary: Google caught hackers using AI to discover and exploit a zero-day vulnerability — because apparently skynet decided to start with cybercrime instead of nuclear war. This is the first confirmed case of AI-powered zero-day discovery in the wild, and it's absolutely terrifying.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas got absolutely wrecked by ransomware, taking down education across the entire US while attackers defaced login pages with ransom demands. Millions of students and teachers locked out because EdTech security is apparently still stuck in 2003.

articles.title: Broken Promises: RIP Instagram’s End-to-End Encrypted DMs
articles.summary: Microsoft's April patch bonanza fixed 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. Meanwhile Chrome patched its fourth zero-day of the year because browsers are basically digital swiss cheese.

articles.title: Google disrupts hackers using AI to exploit an unknown weakness in a company's digital defense
articles.summary: The Mini Shai-Hulud worm is back and hungrier than ever, compromising npm packages from TanStack, Mistral AI, and others in a fresh supply chain massacre. TeamPCP continues their reign of terror across the open source ecosystem.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram just killed its end-to-end encrypted DMs feature, breaking years of privacy promises to users. Meta decided that actually implementing real encryption was too hard, so they're just giving up entirely.

articles.title: EFF Launches New Offline Campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid
articles.summary: Finally, some good news: Apple and Android now support end-to-end encrypted RCS messaging between platforms. After years of green bubble shame, iPhone and Android users can finally have private conversations without Big Tech reading over their shoulders.

articles.title: Canada’s Bill C-22 Is a Repackaged Version of Last Year’s Surveillance Nightmare
articles.summary: EFF drops a comprehensive guide for circumventing internet shutdowns, because authoritarian governments keep pulling the plug on democracy. Essential reading for anyone who believes information wants to be free, especially when tyrants say it shouldn't be.

articles.title: It's Patch Tuesday for Microsoft and Not a Zero-Day In Sight
articles.summary: Canada's Bill C-22 is last year's surveillance nightmare in a fresh coat of paint, doubling down on border security theater that tramples digital rights. Because apparently the first version wasn't dystopian enough for Ottawa's taste.

articles.title: Canvas breach spotlights cybercriminal appetite for student data
articles.summary: Checkmarx's official Jenkins plugin got compromised with an infostealer, proving that even security companies can't secure their own supply chains. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a CVE.

articles.title: Hegseth Asks for More Money as Iran War Costs Skyrocket
articles.summary: FBI quietly closed their investigation into Mahmoud Khalil while he rotted in ICE detention, finding no credible threat despite the Trump administration's fear-mongering. Classic case of government agencies manufacturing terrorism where none exists.
